printed_headline_estimate: Tobit regressions of voluntary 3-month household O&M cash (CASHCONT, ETB) and labour (LABORCONT, days) contributions (N = 160 surveyed households across 16 systems; uncensored N = 140 for cash [chi2 = 72.03, Pseudo R2 = 0.12] and N = 135 for labour [chi2 = 76.22, Pseudo R2 = 0.15]; Table 4, PDF p. 10 / p. 994; marginal effects in Table 5, PDF p. 13 / p. 997; SEs not printed): Participation in project design/implementation (DPARDPIMP): cash beta = 0.45 (p < 0.01), dy/dx = 0.37 ETB/month; labour beta = 0.18 (p < 0.05), dy/dx = 0.13 days/month. Health-promoter advocacy (ADVOCACY): cash beta = 0.12 (ns), dy/dx = 0.10; labour beta = 0.32 (p < 0.01), dy/dx = 0.22 days/month. Trust in WUCs (TOWUCs): cash beta = 0.19 (p < 0.10), dy/dx = 0.16; labour beta = -0.05 (ns), dy/dx = -0.03. Household income (INCOME, per ETB 1,000): cash beta = 0.03 (p < 0.10), dy/dx = 0.03; labour beta = 0.04 (p < 0.01), dy/dx = 0.03. No household or community water access/service outcome is estimated.
publication_year_note: Published in Water Policy Vol. 15 (2013), pp. 985-1000 (© IWA Publishing 2013; PDF p. 1); received 17 October 2012, accepted 4 March 2013, available online 24 July 2013 (PDF p. 16). Both issue year and online-first year are 2013.
rationale: Full text (17 PDF pages) is accessible and reports inferential Tobit regressions (Table 4, p. 994; Table 5, p. 997; N = 160 households across 16 rural water systems in Achefer, Ethiopia). However, the study fails Criterion 4 (and narrow Criterion 2) for SWiM synthesis: the sole dependent variables in the econometric models are households' voluntary cash contributions (CASHCONT, in ETB) and voluntary labour contributions (LABORCONT, in days) over the preceding 3 months toward system protection and maintenance (described by the authors as willingness-to-pay cash and willingness-to-contribute labour). No household or community water supply service access outcome (such as connection, coverage, functionality/reliability, continuity, quantity, water quality, or affordability/exclusion) is analysed as a dependent variable (subjective water satisfaction WASATS and perceived source safety PSOWS enter only as explanatory covariates predicting O&M contributions and are statistically insignificant). Moreover, the main significant predictors (self-rated degree of participation during NGO project design/implementation, health-promoter advocacy, household income, and trust in WUCs) are participatory project-delivery, attitudinal, and socioeconomic factors rather than a rule-type legal/administrative/tariff/tenure exposure tested on service access.
